summary: Kimberley C. Patton is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992), where she later served as Assistant Professor (~1993–1999) and Professor (~2005).

Kimiaki Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, under Ratnakaji Bajracharya, and at the University of Oxford (1993). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, and Keio University.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a computational linguistics scholar who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and as director of the BAULT research community (~2008–2013).
Kin Cheung works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leipzig University, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco (2009).

King Pong Chiu is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).

Kirby Flower Smith was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).

Kirill Solonin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts as Professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and as professor at Renmin University of China (~2013).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indology scholar who completed his studies at Presidency College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under multiple teachers, including Madhusudana Nyayacharya, Gopinath Bhattacharyya, and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He taught at the Fourth Higher School and served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973) and served as professor at Shitennoji University (~1974–2008) and director of the Shitennoji Research Institute of Buddhist Doctrine (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Otani University (1927–1931) under Enga Teramoto. He held posts at Higashi Honganji Kobe Betsuin (1935) and Kōjō Girls' Vocational School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920). He later held posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University (~1925–1927).

Kiyoshi Okano works in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as assistant professor (attested 2002) and as professor in Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He later held posts at Rissho University (attested 1990, 2001) and the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).
Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929). He held posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Tokyo, where he taught (1983–2001), and served as president of Tsurumi Women's University (~2001–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1980–1987) and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1987–1989), and served as assistant professor at Hokkaido University (~1993–2004) and professor at Tohoku University (~2004–2019).

Kiyozō Kazama is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Takatsu, and at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.
